interest: This document is valuable to historians as a concise record of American intelligence gathering on the Japanese economy immediately prior to the Pacific War. It demonstrates the State Department's keen attention to Japan's precarious gold and foreign exchange position at the close of 1939, as well as Japanese government efforts to extract defense financing from emigrant communities in the Philippines through bond sales in Iloilo. Additionally, the cross-reference notations offer researchers clear archival pathways to locate related reports dispersed across other State Department decimal classifications.
overview: This file consists of a Department of State List of Papers (Form DS-46) documenting records under decimal file 894.51 (Japanese Financial Conditions) from late 1939 to February 1940. The sheet indexes three items: a report prepared by George F. Luthringer and transmitted by Herbert Feis concerning Japanese gold and foreign exchange resources at the end of 1939; a despatch from U.S. Ambassador to Japan Joseph C. Grew enclosing a monthly report and memorandum on Japanese financial affairs for November 1939; and a telegram from Francis B. Sayre, U.S. High Commissioner to the Philippine Islands, regarding the importation of eight Japanese government bonds at the port of Iloilo to collect national defense funds from Japanese residents in the Philippines. Because the underlying papers were cross-referenced or transferred to other decimal files (including 894.515, 894.5151, 894.00 P.R./144, and 711.00111 a), this list of papers sheet represents the sole document in the file.

The entries include a report on Japanese gold and foreign exchange resources at the end of 1939 prepared by Mr. Luthringer and transmitted by Herbert Feis, a despatch from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew enclosing a financial report for November 1939, and a telegram from High Commissioner Francis B. Sayre regarding the importation of Japanese government bonds into Iloilo, Philippines, to raise national defense funds.
